# Quick Summary — Unit 6: Animal Tissue
### Persona: Beginner | D_target: 2 | Word Count: ~782

---

## 1. History & Overview

- **Xavier Bichat** (1771–1802) coined 'tissue'; is both **Father** and **Founder** of animal histology; distinguished **21 types** of elementary tissues — without a microscope.
- **Karl Mayer** (1801) coined the term **'histology'**; **Marcello Malpighi** (1628–1694) is the **Founder of histology**.
- **Phylum Coelenterata** = first phylum with **tissue / tissue grade of organization**.
- Animal tissues are four types: **Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, and Nervous** (classified by origin, structure, location, function).

## 2. Epithelial Tissue

- **Covering, lining, forming, and secreting tissue** — covers body surfaces, lines cavities, forms glands, secretes enzymes/hormones.
- **Avascular** (no blood vessels) — nutrition and gas exchange by **diffusion**; rests on **basement membrane** (white collagen).
- **Minimal matrix**; cells held by **4 junctions**: Tight, Adherens, Desmosome, Gap.
- **Surfaces by coelom**: Acoelomate = 2; Pseudocoelomate = 3; Coelomate = 4.
- **Origin**: all three germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm).

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="All four historians + tissue grade hierarchy overview" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

**Classification by Layers:**

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Phylum Coelenterata and the evolution of tissue organization" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Epithelial Tissue]
  A --> B[Simple / Single Layer]
  A --> C[Compound / Multiple Layers]
  B --> D[Squamous]
  B --> E[Cuboidal]
  B --> F[Columnar]
  B --> G[Pseudostratified]
  C --> H[Stratified]
  C --> I[Transitional]
```

## 3. Connective Tissue

- **Most abundant** animal tissue; originated from **mesoderm**.
- Has **fewer cells**, **most abundant matrix**, and **abundant fibres**.
- **Three sub-types**:

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="General features of epithelial tissue (all key properties combined)" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Connective Tissue]
  A --> B[Proper CT — binds]
  A --> C[Supportive CT — supports]
  A --> D[Fluid CT — circulates]
  B --> B1[Loose Matrix]
  B --> B2[Dense Matrix]
  C --> C1[Cartilage — avascular]
  C --> C2[Bone — vascular]
  D --> D1[Blood]
  D --> D2[Lymph]
```

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Avascular nature + diffusion-based nutrition" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

- **CT Fibres**: Collagen = **White**, inelastic, in bundles | Elastic = **Yellow**, branched | Reticulate = **Colourless**, forms stroma.
- **Blood**: Plasma **55%** + Blood cells **45%** (RBCs, WBCs, Platelets).

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Guide to simple epithelial tissues overview" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

## 4. Muscular Tissue- **Contractile tissue**; mesodermal origin.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Compound epithelial tissues overview" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Muscular Tissue] --> B[Skeletal / Voluntary\nFatigues immediately]
  A --> C[Smooth / Involuntary\nFatigues after 10-12 hrs]
  A --> D[Cardiac / Involuntary\nNever fatigues]
```

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="CT Components: Cells + Matrix + Fibres" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

- **Cardiac muscle** has **intercalated discs** separating cardiocytes.
- **Red muscle** = with myoglobin (man, goat); **White muscle** = without myoglobin (athletes, fish).

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Proper connective tissue infographic" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

## 5. Nervous Tissue

- **Controls, coordinates, integrates, and regulates**; **ectodermal** in origin.
- **Two cell types**:
  - **Neuroglia** — supportive, non-neuronal, **can do mitosis**.
  - **Neurone** — structural + functional unit, **cannot do mitosis**.
- **Neurone parts**: **Soma** (Cyton) + **Neurites** (Dendrite = afferent/sensory; Axon = efferent/motor).
- **Myelinated** = white, fast conduction, **Nodes of Ranvier** present; **Non-myelinated** = gray, slow.
- **Gray matter** = outer brain + inner spinal cord | **White matter** = inner brain + outer spinal cord.
